name: Deborah
charge: Judging Israel under the palm tree; going up with Barak when he would not go alone
summary: Deborah, a prophetess to whom Israel came for judgment, delivered the Lord's command to Barak and went with him. The Lord defeated the Canaanite host, Jael took Sisera, and Deborah and Barak sang of the deliverance. The land rested forty years.
offense: Deborah was a prophetess, and Israel came to her for judgment under the palm tree between Ramah and Bethel (Judges 4:4-5). In a time when the people had chosen new gods and the highways had become unsafe, she arose as a mother in Israel (Judges 5:6-8). Her service was not merely to comfort an afflicted people. She brought the Lord's command to bear upon their condition. She sent for Barak and told him what the Lord had commanded: gather ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, draw toward Tabor, and meet the host that the Lord would deliver into his hand (Judges 4:6-7). Deborah gave the prophetic direction; Barak gathered and commanded the army. When he made his going dependent upon hers, she accompanied him but did not soften the word concerning the honour he would lose (Judges 4:8-10). Encouragement did not require withholding correction. At the moment of battle she called him to rise because the Lord had gone before him (Judges 4:14). Her confidence rested on the command and promise already given. She did not leave Barak measuring ten thousand men against nine hundred chariots as though those numbers settled the matter. Faithful instruction turned his attention to who had appointed the battle.
judgment: The Lord fulfilled the word: Barak defeated the host, Jael took Sisera, and Jabin was subdued (Judges 4:15-24). Deborah and Barak then sang praise to the Lord. The song begins with the people willingly offering themselves, and her heart is toward the governors who did the same (Judges 5:1-2, 9). Willing service had also marked those who brought offerings for the tabernacle (Exodus 35:21-22). In each service, the heart had to move with the work. The song did not commend everyone without distinction. It remembered Zebulun and Naphtali risking their lives, named the tribes that remained behind, and pronounced the curse upon Meroz for refusing help (Judges 5:15-18, 23). Thanksgiving preserved the judgment as well as the victory. The willing were to be remembered, and the absent were not to borrow their honour. The land rested forty years (Judges 5:31). Deborah's place in the deliverance is established by the work itself: she judged, instructed, accompanied, strengthened, and gave the glory to the Lord. A mother in Israel helped call the nation out of fear and back into service.

verses.text: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time.
And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth–el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh–naphtali, and said unto him, Hath not the Lord God of Israel commanded, saying, Go and draw toward mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
And I will draw unto thee to the river Kishon Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thine hand.
And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.

And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the Lord shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.
And Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and he went up with ten thousand men at his feet: and Deborah went up with him.

entries.commentary: When Ehud was dead, the children of Israel again did evil, and the Most High sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor, whose captain was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles. Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron, and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel, and they cried unto the Most High.

Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, judged Israel at that time, dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment. She calls Barak the son of Abinoam and gives him the commandment of the Most High: draw toward mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, and I will draw unto thee Sisera with his chariots and his multitude to the river Kishon, and deliver him into thine hand. Barak answers, if thou wilt go with me, then I will go, but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go. Deborah agrees to go, but tells him the journey shall not be for his honour, for the Most High shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh and goes up with ten thousand men at his feet, and Deborah goes up with him. Heber the Kenite, of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites and pitched his tent by Kedesh. Sisera gathers all nine hundred chariots of iron unto the river of Kishon, and Deborah says unto Barak, up, for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand; is not the Lord gone out before thee? The Most High discomfits Sisera and all his chariots and all his host with the edge of the sword before Barak; Sisera lights down off his chariot and flees away on his feet, and all his host falls upon the edge of the sword; there was not a man left.

Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber. Jael invites him in, covers him with a mantle, and gives him milk to drink when he asks for water. He tells her to stand in the door and say no man is there; then Jael takes a nail of the tent and a hammer in her hand, goes softly unto him as he sleeps fast and weary, and smites the nail into his temples and fastens it into the ground, and he dies. The word through Deborah stands: Sisera was sold into the hand of a woman. When Barak comes pursuing, Jael shows him Sisera lying dead with the nail in his temples. So God subdued that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel, and their hand prospered and prevailed until they had destroyed him. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)
